extDescription.message: Browser-only VPN client for TrustTunnel (AdGuard) servers: connects as an HTTPS proxy, imports tt:// keys and TOML configs, per-site split tunneling.

errAuth407.message: The server rejected the username/password (407). Check the server credentials.

hintCert.message: Firefox does not trust the server certificate. Settings → “Certificate” next to the server → import the .pem in Firefox: Settings → Privacy & Security → View Certificates → Authorities → Import, and tick “Trust this CA to identify websites”.

hintCertDomain.message: The server certificate is issued for another name — the hostname must match the certificate.

hintCertExpired.message: The server certificate has expired (or the computer clock is wrong).

hintDns.message: Cannot resolve the server name (DNS). Check the hostname.

hintRefused.message: The server refused the connection: the port is closed or the service is not running.

hintTimeout.message: The server does not respond (timeout). The port may be blocked on the way.

hintTlsReset.message: The server dropped the TLS connection. Possible causes: the hostname does not match the server SNI, client_random rules are enabled on the server, or http1/http2 is disabled.

hintBadGateway.message: The server could not reach the site (error on the VPN server side).

errTimeout.message: The server did not respond within 10 s.

errSocks.message: No connection through local SOCKS5 $1. Is trusttunnel_client running?

errNetwork.message: Could not connect to the server. Check the address and port, trust in the (self-signed) certificate, the username/password, and that http1 or http2 is enabled on the server.

errNoServer.message: No server selected. Add one in the settings.

errNoBackground.message: The background script did not respond.

errLinkBase64.message: The tt:// link is corrupted: invalid base64.

errNotLink.message: This is not a tt:// link.

errSubscriptionOnly.message: The config only contains subscription_url — such keys are not supported yet.

errNoHostname.message: The config has no server hostname.

warnSni.message: Firefox cannot use custom_sni ($1) — the hostname will be used instead.

warnClientRandom.message: client_random cannot be set in a browser: if the server requires it, the connection will fail.

warnCert.message: The server uses its own (self-signed) certificate: Firefox must trust it — see “Certificate” next to the server.

warnSkipVerify.message: skip_verification does not work in a browser: the server certificate must be trusted.

warnHttp3.message: Browsers do not use HTTP/3 for proxies — http1 or http2 must be enabled on the server.

warnIpHost.message: The hostname is an IP address: TrustTunnel requires SNI with a domain name, the connection may fail.

warnSocksListener.message: The config has [listener.socks] $1 — you can use the “via local trusttunnel_client” mode.

modeExclude.message: Everything via VPN except the list

popupAddServer.message: Add a server in the settings

toastListUpdated.message: List updated. Reload the tab to apply.

optIntro.message: Browser-only VPN. Firefox connects to your TrustTunnel (AdGuard) server directly as an HTTPS proxy — nothing else to install.

optKeyLabel.message: tt:// key or TOML config (trusttunnel_client.toml or trusttunnel_endpoint --format toml export)

optKeyPlaceholder.message:
tt://?AAEC…

or

[endpoint]
hostname = "vpn.example.com"
addresses = ["203.0.113.10:443"]
username = "user"
password = "…"

kindDirectHint.message: Recommended. Needs a domain hostname with a trusted certificate (Let's Encrypt, or an imported self-signed one) and http1 or http2 enabled on the server.

kindSocksHint.message: For HTTP/3, anti-DPI, client_random. You run the client yourself with a [listener.socks] section.

optPassHint.message: Leave the password empty to keep the saved one.

optStorageHint.message: Credentials are stored in this Firefox profile (storage.local) only.

optNoServers.message: No servers yet — paste a tt:// key or a config below.

btnCertTitle.message: Save the server certificate (.pem) to import into Firefox

confirmDelete.message: Delete server “$1”? Its username and password will be removed.

errNoCert.message: This server has no saved certificate.

toastCertSaved.message: Certificate saved. Import it in Firefox: Settings → Privacy & Security → View Certificates → Authorities → Import, tick “Trust this CA to identify websites”.

errPasteKey.message: Paste a tt:// key or a TOML config.

toastFieldsFilled.message: Fields filled in. Check them and click “Save server”.

errFileTooBig.message: The file is too large for a config.

toastSavedButFailed.message: Server saved, but the connection failed: $1

toastImportCert.message: This server has its own certificate — click “Certificate” and import it into Firefox.

modeExcludeHint.message: Sites from the exclusion list open directly.

listHint.message: One domain per line. A domain includes all its subdomains. IPv4 addresses and CIDR subnets are allowed. Lines starting with # are ignored.

optKillSwitch.message: Kill switch: if the server is unreachable, do not let traffic bypass the VPN

optWebrtc.message: Prevent IP leaks through WebRTC while the VPN is on

optDnsHint.message: Names of sites routed via VPN are resolved on the server side (the CONNECT request carries the site name).

helpCert.message: Direct mode requires Firefox to trust the server certificate. Let's Encrypt works out of the box. For a self-signed one: click “Certificate” next to the server, then Firefox Settings → Privacy & Security → View Certificates → Authorities → Import, and tick “Trust this CA to identify websites”. Accepting the risk on a warning page is not enough for proxies.

helpDomain.message: The server checks SNI, so the hostname must be a domain from hosts.toml that resolves to the server address.

helpProto.message: Firefox talks to proxies over HTTP/1.1 or HTTP/2. The server vpn.toml must have [listen_protocols.http1] or [listen_protocols.http2], not only quic.

helpRules.message: If the server rules.toml uses client_random_prefix, a browser cannot satisfy it — use the SOCKS5 mode.

helpSocks.message: Add a [listener.socks] section with address = "127.0.0.1:1080" to trusttunnel_client.toml and run trusttunnel_client --config trusttunnel_client.toml.
